lessons: Tonight's WR went 2-1 with only three real removal spells (two Rebuke, Brimstone Volley) plus narrow Urgent Exorcism, below the guide's five or six; take a second removal over Silverchase Fox or Night Revelers.
Round 1's 0-2 loss to BR came with thin evasion (Abbey Griffin, Falkenrath Marauders) against Bloodline Keeper, two Screeching Bat and Falkenrath Noble; take a third flier over ground filler.
Tonight contradicted the guide's WR warning: our 9 Mountain/8 Plains build went 2-1, winning 2-0 vs UB and G with Bonds of Faith and two Rebuke.
Black was the deep colour in this pod, and a black-based deck of cheap creatures with two Victim of Night and Tribute to Hunger went 6-0 in games.
Take removal early: two Victim of Night made my deck, but seat 3 also ran Victim of Night and Claustrophobia, so removal was contested.
My six-Mountain splash for Geistflame, Bloodcrazed Neonate and Riot Devils went 6-0, but no game tested colour screw, so check the splash count before copying it.
Fliers win this format, as the guide says: our flierless mono-green deck lost all three matches, while our pack 2 first pick Murder of Crows and pack 3 Geist-Honored Monk went unplayed.
Contradicting the guide, Spider Spawning was dead in our mono-green deck with no self-mill enablers; don't count it as late-game value without Armored Skaab or Grasp of Phantoms.
Festerhide Boar, filler per the guide, filled our 23 in mono-green; with no evasion, our 18-28 turn games stalled, so take a second colour with fliers over green filler.
In round 3, the WR deck answered my fliers with Rebuke, Bonds of Faith and Urgent Exorcism, so in UB, prioritize ground blockers and a real finisher over more low-impact fliers or sorceries.
Keeping the curve low left my UB deck stalling into 18–26 turn games; Dissipate, Fortress Crab and the second Lost in the Mist stalled rather than closed, so take threats or removal instead.
Seat 1's BR deck went 3-0 on Victim of Night, Falkenrath Noble, Markov Patrician and Ghoulcaller's Chant, the same black core I drafted; with black contested, lock in removal early.
Tonight's WR went 2-1 with five fliers but only three real removal spells (Harvest Pyre, Into the Maw of Hell, Blazing Torch); take a third removal spell over Unruly Mob.
Tonight contradicted the guide's stranded-pick warning: Into the Maw of Hell was played, but Disciple of Griselbrand and Vampire Interloper were dead picks; stop taking black once red-white is set.
Round 3's 0-2 to BR in 24- and 26-turn games, facing Bloodline Keeper and two Screeching Bat, showed WR lacked card advantage beyond Rally the Peasants; take Mentor of the Meek over a ground body.
Tonight's grindy 18-to-28-turn games exposed my 11-creature WR deck: prioritize evasive threats and card advantage, like Midnight Haunting, over extra Moment of Heroism tricks.
My 0-2 loss to Voiceless Spirit, Chapel Geist and Spectral Rider showed spirit fliers beat me, so value Urgent Exorcism and Geistcatcher's Rig highly as my cleanest flier answers.

Skip self-mill cards outside UG: my UB deck played Armored Skaab, Stitcher's Apprentice and Skaab Goliath with no Spider Spawning, and its 29-, 17- and 29-turn games contradicted the guide's tempo advice.
Take cheap evasive creatures over speculative card-advantage like Think Twice or Curse of Oblivion; my slow UB deck dropped 1-2 to WG and 0-2 to WR without enough early pressure.
Pack 2's early picks Geist of Saint Traft, Snapcaster Mage and Forbidden Alchemy went unplayed; commit to two colours by mid pack 2 instead of hedging across blue and black.
Round 2's 0-2 loss came to flier-heavy WR (Voiceless Spirit x2, Spectral Rider, Chapel Geist); my W/G had only Fiend Hunter and Smite the Monstrous as removal, so prioritise removal over filler.
Green was thin beyond Garruk Relentless, so take second-colour playables over speculative red like Ashmouth Hound and Scourge of Geier Reach, both unplayed.
